title: Hang a telescoping server rail across a rack: latch one end, draw it out and find the same U's holes on the far post
instruction: Mount the rail from the cradle on the near side of the rack, in the free U directly above the installed server, with both end latches engaged, then let go of it.
context: Racking servers is the physical step of every AI cluster build-out: before a server goes in, its two rails are hung inside the rack's posts at the planned U. A tool-less rail's ends carry square pegs for the posts' 9.5 mm square holes and a spring catch that clicks when the end is pushed home. The closed rail is shorter than the rack depth, so one end is pegged and latched first, then the telescoping member is drawn out and its pegs found in the other post at the same U, 0.84 m away: unlike a front-only panel, the far end's U must be found again after the rail is drawn out, with the near end already latched. The two pegs sit 31.75 mm apart, which matches only one U's top and bottom holes, at 0.25 mm play; an end one U off gives a sloped rail the server will not slide on. Here the target is the free U directly above an already installed 1U server, which changes per trial; the posts carry U numbers. A latch needs a push of more than about 10 N over its last 2.5 mm.
setup: Station table in front of two YAM arms (bases 61 cm apart), overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Positions in cm: x forward from the line between the arm bases, y to the robot's left of their midpoint. (1) 12U four-post open-frame rack (StarTech.com 4POSTRACK12U, black steel) through-bolted to the bench at four corners on its base frame (casters off), side open toward the robot, mounting depth set to 84 cm: near-side rear post at y +42 (robot's left), near-side front post at y -42, their square-hole EIA-310 flanges (9.5 mm holes, 3 per U) facing each other, hole column at x 30; U numbers and U boundary ticks printed in white on each post's robot-facing leg; U1's lower boundary 1.2 cm above the table; far-side posts 46.5 cm further in x. (2) A 1U server (760 mm deep, lid rendered blue for contrast) already installed on its own rails across the front and rear posts at U1, U2 or U3, its near-side rail latched at both ends. (3) The 1.45 kg telescoping training rail fabricated to fixture/assembly.md and the two supplied DXF drawings, closed (80 cm bracket face to bracket face, 8 cm travel), lying upright in a foam cradle on the table at x 19, y 0, parallel to y, rear end (red label) toward the rear post, front end (blue label) toward the front post. Each end bracket has two 9 mm square pegs 31.75 mm apart and a spring latch with a flag (orange out = open, green flush = latched). Per trial (from the seed): installed server at U1, U2 or U3 (the target is the U above), rack moved 4-8 mm in x and up to 6 mm in y, cradle moved up to 10 mm in x, 12 mm in y and 3 deg. Named setups: see README; the screenshot shows setup 0 (target U3).
scoring: Read at the end of the trial (person check in brackets). 0 if either end is latched or pegged in the flange holes at any U other than the target (sloped or misplaced rail; read the printed U next to the pegs). 0.25: one end latched at the target U (flag green, end does not come off under a 15 N axial pull for 1 s). 0.5: one end latched and the other end's pegs in the target U's holes but not latched; or both latched with a hand on or within 10 cm of the rail. 1.0 (ends the trial): both ends latched at the target U, both hands 10 cm or more from the rail, rail still for 1 s. Otherwise 0 (rail in the cradle or in the air, pegs not in).
reset_notes: Press each latch release and lift the rail off the posts, close it fully and lay it in the cradle (labels as in setup). Move the installed server on its rails to the next setup's U, and the rack and cradle to the setup's marks. Setups run in order 0-4.
fidelity: Isaac Lab-Arena yam_arena, PhysX (CPU) 240 Hz, 20 Hz control, full size. Rail members are free rigid bodies on a prismatic joint; pegs in square holes by contact (0.25 mm play). Computed forces stand in for the slide drag (4 N) and each spring latch (10 N push-back over the last 2.5 mm, then held); both replica calibration targets. The force cap is numerical. Rack on the table so U2-U4 are in reach; installed server simplified to a box. No welds or proximity rules. Full statement: README.
run_limit: 2400 control steps (2 min at 20 Hz). The trial also ends as soon as the score reaches 1.0.
scores: Dream-1 returned no usable action on seed 0. Inspect Robots completed 32 warm-up steps and produced no task score. Scripted reference: 1.0 in the official Inspect Robots run.
no_model_video_reason: Only the camera warm-up was recorded before the first model action. PolicyError: q_r_chunk gripper leaves 0..1: [-0.123, 0.913]
